body:
maya: Quick design check — proposing a compact progress "pill" at the top of the console on first-run. Shows 3 small pills: Setup, Sample project, Quick tour. Persistent but dismissible. Thoughts?
sam: I like the visual anchor, but contrast on the mock is too low. small pills + light gray bg fails WCAG for small text.
olivia: Agree re contrast. Also we need a keyboard focus state and clear focus order. Pills must be reachable via Tab.
kai: If we persist it, we should respect a dismiss flag in localStorage and avoid showing after user skips twice. Also consider privacy: no telemetry without consent.
maya: Good point on dismiss logic. UX question: should pills expand to show micro-copy on hover/long-press? Mobile is tight.
sam: Hover -> tooltip on desktop, long-press or tap-to-expand on mobile. Ensure tap targets >= 44px.
olivia: Copy brainstorming: 'Complete setup — 3 quick steps' vs 'Get started with your first project' vs 'Finish onboarding'. Which reads best?
kai: 'Get started with your first project' sounds friendlier and sets expectation. 'Complete' sounds like a chore.
maya: Let's A/B test the copy: variation A = 'Get started', variation B = 'Complete setup — 3 quick steps'. We'll track clicks and completion.
design-bot: Experiment created: onboard_pill_copy_A (Get started) vs onboard_pill_copy_B (Complete setup). Metric: funnel_onboard_pill_clicks, funnel_onboard_completion.
jim: Accessibility nit: add aria-live updates when a step completes, aria-labels for each pill, and announce when the pill is dismissed. Also ensure color alone isn't the only state.
maya: Noted — will add live region and icons + text. I'll update Figma with high-contrast palette and keyboard flows.
sam: tiny: add an accessible close 'x' that is keyboard operable and has aria-label="Dismiss onboarding helper".
olivia: Also include a 'Why this helps' inline link in the expanded state explaining telemetry + local opt-out.
maya: Cool—I'll iterate and post updated frames in #design when ready. Targeting a first-pass prototype in next sprint. Thanks everyone! :rocket:
